subject: Materials Science
title: Decellularized Tissue Scaffolds
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Decellularized Tissue Scaffolds.

hook.text: Take a pig's heart, wash out all its cells, and you're left with a perfect ghost scaffold — ready for human cells.

buildup.text: Decellularization removes all cellular material using detergents — leaving behind the extracellular matrix intact.

discovery.text: The remaining matrix retains growth factors, mechanical properties, and architecture — nature's perfect scaffold.

twist.text: Incomplete decellularization leaves DNA behind — triggering immune rejection when implanted.

climax.text: Decellularized skin, heart valves, and bladder patches are FDA-approved and used in thousands of surgeries annually.

punchline.text: Nature built the scaffold — we just clean it out and move new tenants in.

quiz.question: What remains after decellularization of a tissue?
options: Only the cells with no structural support
The extracellular matrix with its structure and growth factors intact
